item.title: VA Electronic Health Record Modernization: System Deployed to 13 Sites in 2026 and Work Planned to Continue at an Accelerated Pace
item.description:
What GAO Found
In 2017, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) began its most recent effort to modernize its legacy electronic health records (EHR) system. After a 3-year pause to make improvements, VA deployed the new EHR to all 13 planned medical centers in 2026. The pace of these 2026 deployments (13 live sites in 6 months) was considerably faster than the deployment of the six original sites between October 2020 and March 2024. The department intends to continue this accelerated pace, with 26 system deployments planned for 2027.
Department of Veterans Affairs’ (VA) Electronic Health Record System Deployments in 2026
The department relied on standardized processes and workflows for the accelerated deployments. According to VA officials, data from post-deployment assessments demonstrate that the four Michigan medical centers are generally meeting performance metric targets, which indicates to them that sites are generally able to serve veterans as they did prior to the deployments. However, a survey of user satisfaction is not yet complete.
From June 2020 to March 2025, GAO issued five reports on VA’s efforts to implement its EHR system. In these reports, GAO made 18 recommendations. While VA has taken steps to address some recommendations, the department has not fully implemented 11 of the 18. In particular, GAO’s preliminary results show that, as of November 2026, VA has not yet demonstrated that it employed leading scheduling practices for the EHR modernization program as GAO has previously recommended. It has not developed a complete integrated master schedule incorporating the entire required scope of work or detailed documentation for scheduled activities.
Fully implementing GAO’s recommendations would help ensure that the program is well positioned to support its accelerated deployments. It is critically important that VA update its integrated schedule to inform decision-making and allow the department and Congress to understand tradeoffs that must be made to complete deployments by 2031.
Why GAO Did This Study
VA’s health care system provides services to more than 9 million veterans. VA has been working to replace its legacy EHR system with a modernized, commercial system. In April 2023, after deploying the new system to five of its medical centers, VA paused deployments to address user concerns and ensure patient safety. In 2024, VA announced the restart of deployment activities with 13 sites in 2026, beginning with four sites in Michigan. VA plans to complete 170 site deployments by 2031.
GAO was asked to testify on VA’s progress deploying its new EHR system to medical facilities in 2026 and the status of open GAO recommendations related to VA’s EHR modernization.
GAO summarized the preliminary results of a draft report currently with the agency for comment that addresses, among other things, VA’s progress deploying the new EHR in 2026 and VA’s scheduling practices. GAO also summarized the status of VA’s actions to implement recommendations made in five prior reports.
